features.title: Secondhand windows
features.description: Josh says the upstairs windows were bought secondhand. Their panes and frames are visible; the purchase history is spoken evidence.
features.unknown: Dimensions and performance have not been independently measured.
features.review: checked against sampled visuals and captions by Codex; not an independent audit

features.title: Masonry and thermal mass
features.description: Josh describes an insulated-concrete-form structure with concrete between insulation layers and credits that thermal mass with moderating indoor temperature.
features.unknown: The complete wall assembly is not visible in the finished room; thermal performance is a speaker claim.
features.review: checked against sampled visuals and captions by Codex; not an independent audit

features.title: Dark tiled floor
features.description: The tiled floor is visible. Josh says its dark color was chosen to absorb winter sun, while the higher summer sun should avoid heating it.
features.unknown: Dimensions and performance have not been independently measured.
features.review: checked against sampled visuals and captions by Codex; not an independent audit

features.title: Locally milled white-oak beam
features.description: Josh identifies a kitchen beam as white oak milled on the property with a chainsaw mill, and mentions continued drying and warping.
features.unknown: Species and milling history come from narration. The beam has not been measured.
features.review: checked against sampled visuals and captions by Codex; not an independent audit

features.title: Exposed red-oak ceiling beams
features.description: Josh identifies the overhead beams as red oak from the property and says they were waxed. The repeated exposed beams are clearly visible.
features.unknown: Dimensions and performance have not been independently measured.
features.review: checked against sampled visuals and captions by Codex; not an independent audit

features.title: Upstairs wood stove
features.description: A separate stove is visible upstairs. Josh says they use this one less after becoming grid tied. It is a different stove from the downstairs thermosiphon stove.
features.unknown: No upstairs hot-water connection is established by this passage.
features.review: checked against sampled visuals and captions by Codex; not an independent audit

features.title: Gated passage to the older home
features.description: Josh identifies a gated opening as the passage to the original earth-sheltered home below. Its existence is supported; its full path is not recovered.
features.unknown: The connecting staircase is not fully shown. The film does not establish the route below the opening.
features.review: checked against sampled visuals and captions by Codex; not an independent audit

features.title: Walnut staircase
features.description: The walk upstairs shows a timber staircase. Josh identifies the wood as black walnut milled on the property.
features.unknown: The full stair dimensions and all landings are unknown.
features.review: checked against sampled visuals and captions by Codex; not an independent audit

features.title: Lighter upper-floor construction
features.description: Josh explains the transition from ICF construction to six-inch conventional framing on the upper floor, where he says there are three bedrooms.
features.unknown: Bedroom interiors and their complete arrangement are not shown.
features.review: checked against sampled visuals and captions by Codex; not an independent audit

features.title: Original earth-sheltered home
features.description: The lower masonry home preceded the chalet. Josh says it is dug into the hill with earth on three sides and an open south side.
features.unknown: Historical construction views and present-day views are kept separate.
features.review: checked against sampled visuals and captions by Codex; not an independent audit

subject.gist: A former Army Ranger and his family built underground for security, slept through a tornado, and traded social time for tending their farm.

story.text: Josh, a former Army Ranger, and Chiara want their children to know where their food comes from and their family to be ready for hard times. They build a room at a time as money allows, starting underground and adding a chalet with timber from their land. Their solid shelter lets them sleep through a tornado. Farming brings harder bargains: cattle and hay cannot wait for a free weekend, and social time suffers. What amazes Josh most is watching the children absorb years of practical lessons. His measure of wealth is the life thriving around them, and his advice is to keep encouraging it.
